sources.title: P. Bhaskar Reddy, South Indian kingdoms: Pallavas and Chalukyas, INFLIBNET
sources.note: Indexed institutional chapter, sections 3.2-3.3 and introduction. Used for expansion and broad political transition, not the discredited identification of an Ajanta painting as a Persian embassy. Approximate 750s ending accommodates ASI’s 757 royal-seat endpoint.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Jaina, Shaiva and Vaishnava Caves, Badami
sources.note: Directly read historical and architectural sections. Cliff inscription 543; Pallava occupation 642 to mid-650s; royal seat until 757. Surviving fortifications span sixth-sixteenth centuries. Avoid erroneous page latitude and universal peace/tolerance claims.

sources.title: UNESCO, Group of Monuments at Pattadakal
sources.note: Direct description, seventh-eighth-century architecture, Lokamahadevi and Virupaksha around 740. Jain sanctuary in present group is not automatically Early Chalukya.

sources.title: Suganya, Harshavardhan and Rajani, Hydrological maps as a tool for the exploration of historical water systems at Badami (2022)
sources.note: Direct publisher abstract read; full article subscription restricted. Abstract explicitly identifies cliff-cut and masonry channels as Chalukyan, aqueduct as Vijayanagara, and describes remote sensing, terrain models and wider catchment. No claims beyond accessible abstract.

sources.title: Meghana Kuppa and Srikumar M. Menon, Stories from Silent Stones (2018)
sources.note: Direct original 49-page paper, especially printed 440-445, PDF indices 2-7. Shankaralingana Gundu staged wedge-hole preparation, steel wedge and hammer, comparison with later stoneworking. Dating method treated as authors’ proposal, not universal diagnostic.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Badami Cave III
sources.note: Direct institutional site account. Dedication 578, Mangalesha under Kirtivarman I, village endowment, artist names, surviving painting of royal couple watching dance. Explicitly before imported 600 start.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Virupaksha Temple, Pattadakal
sources.note: Direct site account: Lokamahadevi patronage, Gunda-Anivaritachari and Sarvasiddhi-Achari, royal honors, narrative panels and date around 740.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Pattadakal monolithic pillar inscription
sources.note: Direct description of eighth-century pillar: Jnanasivacharya’s origin north of Ganga, purchase from Aryabhatta of 30 nivarttanas, subsequent temple endowment. No conversion of land unit into acres or identification with earlier mathematician.

sources.title: Odile Divakaran, Le temple de Jambuliṅga à Bādāmi (1970)
sources.note: Original scholarly article: direct page 15; indexed original page 17 via query with pageId=T1_17 verified Vinayavati’s installation of three images in 699 during her son Vijayaditya’s reign, and porch with connecting stone bench.

sources.title: F. Kielhorn, Aihole Inscription of Pulikesin II, Epigraphia Indica VI, pages 1-12
sources.note: Original edition read through full text mirror: introductory date 634-635, Roman transcription page 4, translation page 7, literary discussion pages 3-4, verses 35-37 page 12. Original record uses early regional southern script; public sample explicitly a scholarly Roman transliteration.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Jaina Narayana Temple, Pattadakal
sources.note: Direct institutional monument account: probably ninth century, Rashtrakuta period, over earlier brick Jain temple. Later phase explicitly separated.

proposedOverrides.name: Chalukyas of Badami
proposedOverrides.summary: A Deccan power centered on Badami, with influential architecture and water engineering.

batchIdentityNotes.scope: Early Chalukyas of Badami/Vatapi, sixth-eighth centuries. Do not share with existing later Kalyani card chalukya-empire, or assume eastern Vengi line is identical.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: Imported broad Deccan polygons are approximate snapshots, not proof of uniformly direct control or of imperial survival to800. They cross periods of occupation and restoration; overview and ending warn about temporal mismatch. Historical transition753 versus last royal-seat757 is made explicit, without claiming all independence ended on one exact day.
batchIdentityNotes.collision: Exact ID found in index; no runtime card, override or staged bundle at claim time. Existing later Western Chalukya narrative inspected for identity distinction.
